articles.title: Current Challenges and Future Directions for Patient-Reported Outcome Measures in Orthopaedic Research.
articles.authors: Parry JA, Slobogean GP, O'Hara NN
articles.population: Orthopaedic surgery patients
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) in orthopaedic research, including their challenges and future directions
articles.take_home: Patient-reported outcome measures are widely used in orthopaedic surgery but face challenges such as low participation rates, use of measures not designed for specific patient groups, difficulty comparing individual patient recovery, and poor detection of treatment differences in adverse events. The review recommends using PROMs within composite outcomes frameworks to make research more meaningful for both patients and doctors.

articles.title: The Intersection of Mental Health and Orthopaedic Trauma Outcomes.
articles.authors: Vallier HA
articles.population: Patients with orthopaedic trauma
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcome measures and their impact on trauma recovery, screening for posttraumatic stress disorder, anxiety and depression
articles.take_home: Trauma patients often develop psychological problems like post-traumatic stress disorder, anxiety or depression alongside their physical injuries. Trauma centres should offer supportive recovery programmes that use patient-reported outcome measures to identify and monitor these mental health conditions.

articles.title: Impact of Social Determinants of Health on Patient-Reported Outcome Measures and Survey Completion in Orthopaedic Trauma.
articles.authors: Zeller NP, Thomas GM, Rivard RL, Vang S, Peterson TA, Agoro KS, et al.
articles.population: Orthopaedic trauma surgical patients
articles.outcomes: Completion of PROMIS Global Health 10 surveys and PROMIS outcome scores stratified by race/ethnicity and Area Deprivation Index
articles.take_home: Patients from certain ethnic backgrounds and those living in more deprived areas were less likely to complete health surveys after orthopaedic trauma and also reported worse health outcomes. The study highlights that targeted support is needed to help these groups engage with outcome measurement and improve their recovery.

articles.title: Quantifying the Impact of Postoperative Complications Using PROMIS-Global Physical Health Scores in Orthopaedic Trauma Patients.
articles.authors: Thomas GM, Zeller NP, Dornan LD, Rivard RL, Vang S, Agoro KS, et al.
articles.population: Orthopaedic trauma patients aged 18-103 with operative injuries; 62.1% female; average age 58.4 years
articles.outcomes: PROMIS-Global Physical Health (PROMIS-GPH) scores at 6 weeks, 3 months, 6 months and 1 year; major complications (reoperation or readmission within specified timeframes); minor complications (symptomatic hardware removal or emergency department visits)
articles.take_home: Patients who had complications after orthopaedic trauma surgery had significantly lower physical health scores than those without complications. Those with major complications were more likely to report poor physical health outcomes, with low health scores being a predictor of serious complications.

articles.title: The Emergence of Patient Reported Outcomes for the Chest Wall: A PRO Frontier for Orthothoracic Surgery.
articles.authors: Xu JL, Winter JD, Cole PA
articles.population: Patients with chest wall injuries
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcomes (PROs) for chest wall injury, including the Chest Wall Injury Quality of Life questionnaire (C-QoL) and other general health measures
articles.take_home: Most patient-reported outcome tools currently used for chest wall injuries are general health questionnaires that do not capture the specific problems patients experience. A new chest wall-specific questionnaire called C-QoL has been developed, but the field needs more standardised and specialised tools to properly measure how chest wall injuries affect patients' lives.

articles.title: Selecting Appropriate Patient-Reported Outcome Measures in Orthopaedic Trauma: A Framework With Foot and Ankle Trauma as a Case Example.
articles.authors: Schweser KM
articles.population: Orthopaedic trauma patients, specifically foot and ankle trauma as a case example
articles.outcomes: Framework for selecting appropriate patient-reported outcome measures in orthopaedic trauma
articles.take_home: Choosing the right patient questionnaire for measuring recovery after injury is important because using the wrong one may miss important aspects of how patients are doing, give misleading results, and lead to poor clinical decisions. This review provides guidance to help surgeons pick the best questionnaire for their patients.

articles.title: Utility of Patient-Reported Outcome Measures in Clinical Trauma Practice.
articles.authors: Agoro KS, Shapiro LM, Jones CB, Cunningham BP
articles.population: Orthopaedic trauma patients
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported outcomes including pain, functional recovery, and quality of life
articles.take_home: Patient-reported outcome measures help capture how trauma affects patients' pain, function and quality of life beyond what traditional clinical tests show, and can guide treatment decisions that better match what patients actually want to achieve. Despite practical challenges in collecting this information, these measures are becoming an important part of trauma care.

articles.title: Lessons Learned from Patient-Reported Outcome Measure Databases for Orthopaedic Trauma Patients: A Rapid Scoping Review.
articles.authors: Saxby NE, Wilson P, Saxby SM, Malloy M, Bagley P, Miller AN
articles.study_type: Scoping review of databases collecting patient-reported outcome measures
articles.population: Orthopaedic trauma patients
articles.sample_size: 24 studies identified for data extraction from 360 initial results
articles.outcomes: Types and frequency of patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs) used in large multicenter orthopaedic trauma databases; most common measures were EQ-5D-3L (70.8%), Glasgow Outcome Scale-Extended, SF-12, and Short Musculoskeletal Function Assessment
articles.take_home: Very few large databases collect patient-reported outcome measures for orthopaedic trauma patients, with most research coming from registries in Australia, Sweden, and Norway. The authors recommend developing a dedicated orthopaedic trauma database in the United States to improve patient-centred outcomes research.

articles.title: What Is New With Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System in Orthopaedic Trauma.
articles.authors: Sajid MI, Mir A, Mir HR
articles.population: Patients with orthopaedic trauma including upper extremity, lower extremity, pelvic and paediatric injuries
articles.outcomes: Comparison of Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement Information System (PROMIS) with traditional outcome measures; correlation strength, respondent burden, floor and ceiling effects, and sensitivity
articles.take_home: PROMIS is a newer way of measuring how trauma patients recover that works better than older methods because it asks fewer questions, reduces patient frustration, and picks up improvements that other measures might miss. It also helps identify how patients' life circumstances and mental health affect their recovery.

articles.title: Evolving Management of Hip Fracture Patients on Anticoagulant and Antiplatelet Medications: A 22-Year Cohort Study.
articles.authors: House HE, Schwartz A, Shimizu M, Hong I, Cohen JB, Summers HD, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 55 years or older undergoing operative treatment for hip fractures whilst receiving anticoagulant and/or antiplatelet therapy
articles.outcomes: Time to surgery, perioperative transfusion, readmission, 90-day medical and surgical complications, and 90-day mortality
articles.take_home: The type of blood-thinning medication patients were taking did not affect how quickly they had surgery, their complication rates, or death rates within 90 days. Over the 22-year study period, fewer patients needed blood transfusions and fewer were readmitted to hospital, suggesting improved overall care for hip fracture patients on these medications.

articles.title: Open reduction of the femoral butterfly fragment in closed femoral shaft fractures is associated with a higher rate of reoperation to promote union: a retrospective clinical cohort.
articles.authors: Schlauch AM, Zakusylo A, Ball G, Biedermann B, Onafowokan O, Kennerly V, et al.
articles.population: Adults with closed femoral shaft fractures treated surgically at a single Level I trauma centre
articles.sample_size: 139 patients (99 without butterfly fragment, 40 with butterfly fragment)
articles.outcomes: Primary: reoperation to promote union. Secondary: fracture-related infection and post-operative cortical step sign
articles.take_home: Patients with a butterfly fragment in their femur fracture who had open surgical reduction had a much higher rate of needing further surgery (67% versus 7%), suggesting that leaving the fragment alone without surgery may be better for healing.

articles.title: Association Between Baseline Anemia and Nonunion After Proximal Humerus Fracture Across the Adult Lifespan.
articles.authors: Nakken ER, Mamonov A, Garcia-Canga B, Whitney DG, Lang A, Aibinder WR
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using administrative claims database
articles.population: Adults aged 19 years and over who sustained a proximal humerus fracture
articles.sample_size: 25,109 adults with anemia and 64,389 without anemia
articles.outcomes: Incidence of non-union of proximal humerus fracture from 6 to 18 months post-fracture
articles.take_home: Patients with anemia who are younger or middle-aged (40 to 60 years old) have an increased risk of their proximal humerus fracture not healing properly, but this increased risk does not apply to older patients aged 70 years and above.

articles.title: After-hours hip fracture surgery-influence on reoperation risk, mortality, and surgical complications: a cohort study of 98,607 patients from the Norwegian Hip Fracture Register.
articles.authors: Boutera AT, Dybvik E, Engesaeter LB, Guy P, Kristensen TB, Leer-Salvesen S, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 65 years and over with hip fracture
articles.outcomes: 1-year reoperation risk, 30-day mortality, and intraoperative complications
articles.take_home: Hip fracture surgery performed in the evening or at night did not lead to higher rates of needing further surgery, death within 30 days, or complications during surgery compared with daytime surgery. Nighttime surgery was even associated with slightly lower 30-day mortality.

articles.title: Radiographic Accuracy of Identifying Anterolateral Tibial Plafond Involvement in Pronation External Rotation Ankle Fractures.
articles.authors: Lee CM, Oosten J, Allahverdian A, O'Hara S, Rockov ZA, Audet M, et al.
articles.population: Adults with pronation-external rotation ankle fractures treated surgically
articles.sample_size: 83 fractures (37 with both radiographs and CT scans)
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of plain radiographs versus CT for detecting anterolateral tibial plafond involvement and impaction; surgeon intent to pursue direct visualization and articular reduction
articles.take_home: Plain radiographs miss most cases of anterolateral tibial plafond involvement and impaction in pronation-external rotation ankle fractures, detecting only 21% and 67% of cases respectively compared to CT scans. CT imaging should be considered for these fractures to avoid missing important injuries that may affect treatment decisions.

articles.title: Task-specific gait biomechanics following unilateral iliosacral screw fixation for posterior pelvic ring injury.
articles.authors: Jackle K, Kramer M, Meier MP, Hawellek T, Roch PJ, Homann C, et al.
articles.population: Patients treated with unilateral iliosacral screw fixation for posterior pelvic ring injury compared with healthy controls
articles.outcomes: Pelvic rotation during stair climbing, pelvic tilt during step crossing, lower-limb muscle activation, hip joint contact forces, and L5-S1 joint contact force
articles.take_home: Patients who had pelvic ring surgery showed reduced pelvic rotation when climbing stairs and increased pelvic tilt when stepping sideways, compared with healthy people. However, the study was small and the findings do not prove the surgery caused these movement differences.

articles.title: Translation and cultural adaptation of the Oxford Shoulder Score to Swedish and validation of a new 7-day recall version in patients with a proximal humerus fracture.
articles.authors: Lundin PC, Sundh TFD, Adolfsson LE, Bjornsson Hallgren HC
articles.population: Patients with non-operatively treated proximal humerus fracture
articles.outcomes: Convergent validity with QuickDASH, responsiveness to change, internal consistency, and intra-rater reliability of the Swedish Oxford Shoulder Score
articles.take_home: The Swedish version of the Oxford Shoulder Score works well for measuring shoulder pain and function in patients with broken upper arm bones. A new 7-day version of the score is also reliable and useful for tracking recovery in the early stages after injury.

articles.title: Increased frequency of dislocation following total hip arthroplasty for trauma : an age- and sex-matched cohort study.
articles.authors: Williamson TR, Ali R, Kane N, Meek RMD, Jenkinson MRJ
articles.study_type: Single-centre age- and sex-matched cohort study
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty for neck of femur fracture compared with patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Primary outcome: dislocation rate at one year. Secondary outcomes: all-cause revision, infection, periprosthetic fracture, and mortality at one year and medium-term follow-up
articles.take_home: Patients having hip replacement after a femur fracture had four times higher rates of hip dislocation in the first year compared with those having replacement for arthritis, even though surgeons used special implants designed to reduce dislocation more often in the fracture group. Other complication rates were similar between the groups.

articles.title: Preoperative CT-derived psoas attenuation and correction loss after traumatic thoracolumbar fracture fixation: A construct-dependent association.
articles.authors: Ozdemir M, Latifoglu F, Ugur OT, Peksoy F, Kamasak K
articles.population: Adults with traumatic thoracolumbar fractures (AO Spine A3) treated with posterior pedicle screw fixation
articles.outcomes: Correction loss (difference between postoperative and final follow-up spinal alignment angles); association between preoperative psoas muscle quality and correction loss depending on screw placement strategy
articles.take_home: Preoperative psoas muscle quality was associated with how much spinal alignment was lost after surgery, but only when surgeons did not place screws directly through the fractured bone. Lower muscle quality predicted more alignment loss in these cases, suggesting muscle health might help identify patients who need different surgical approaches.

articles.title: Predictors and clinical outcomes of extubation failure in patients with cervical spinal cord injury.
articles.authors: Yeremian S, Wilensky AH, Kuhls DA, McNickle AG
articles.population: Intubated patients with cervical spinal cord injury
articles.outcomes: Extubation success or failure, length of hospital and ICU stay, mortality
articles.take_home: Patients who failed extubation after cervical spinal cord injury spent longer in hospital and in intensive care, but traditional measures used to assess readiness for extubation did not predict who would fail. Extubations performed outside the intensive care unit may carry higher risk of failure.

articles.title: Comparative mortality of pelvic ring fractures vs. hip fractures in adults >/=55 years: A propensity-matched cohort study.
articles.authors: Sabat L, Johnson M, Pasha M, Perdue P, Zuelzer D
articles.population: Adults aged 55 years and over with hip or pelvic ring fractures
articles.outcomes: 1-year all-cause mortality (primary); 30-day, 90-day, and 2-year mortality (secondary)
articles.take_home: Hip fractures had higher mortality at 1 year compared to pelvic fractures in both treatment groups, but pelvic fractures treated with surgery had higher early death rates within 30 days. The study suggests pelvic fragility fractures need better-defined care pathways similar to those for hip fractures.

articles.title: A bedside score using arrival data to identify major hemorrhage after blunt pelvic ring fracture: Development and validation.
articles.authors: Salman SG, Phadke RA, Carlin T, Rosenfelt T, Ramirez J, Mendez-Reyes JE, et al.
articles.population: Adults with documented blunt pelvic ring fractures
articles.sample_size: 239,736 patients (79,912 in test set; 2019-2024 National Trauma Data Bank)
articles.outcomes: Major hemorrhage (defined as hemorrhage-control procedure, hemorrhagic death, or transfusion of 1000 mL or more or 4 or more units of red blood cells within 4 hours); AUROC 0.882 in test set
articles.take_home: A new bedside scoring system using arrival data was better at identifying major bleeding after pelvic fractures than the shock index alone, correctly identifying 678 additional cases while reducing false alarms. However, the score worked less well in patients with falls, so more testing is needed before it can be used in clinical practice.

articles.title: Does the number of debridement procedures impact risk of infection in open fractures?
articles.authors: Bateman LM, Fisher LA, Diaz-Coto S, O'Hara NN, Bzovsky S, Zura RD, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective secondary analysis of prospectively collected trial data
articles.population: Patients with open fractures
articles.outcomes: Surgical site infection rates stratified by wound contamination level and number of debridement procedures
articles.take_home: More debridement operations were linked with higher infection risk rather than lower risk, particularly in severely contaminated wounds. The study suggests avoiding unnecessary repeated debridement procedures to reduce infection risk.

articles.title: Cone-Beam CT-Guided SpineJack(R) vertebral augmentation: A reproducible technique for accurate pedicular access and implant deployment.
articles.authors: Dien E, Grange S, Mondon P, Peraldi L, Lavigne J, Chalamet B, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing SpineJack vertebral augmentation; median age 45 years; 88.8% had traumatic fractures
articles.outcomes: Technical success rate, vertebral height restoration, complications, procedure duration, radiation exposure, outpatient feasibility
articles.take_home: Cone-beam CT-guided SpineJack augmentation successfully restored vertebral height by an average of 77% of lost height and achieved accurate implant placement in all 178 procedures with no serious complications. Most procedures were completed safely as outpatient treatments without nerve or blood vessel damage.

articles.title: The MIS-Diamond fixation: A minimally invasive diamond-shaped construct for spinopelvic dissociation in polytrauma patients.
articles.authors: Giorgi PD, Ramponi A, Legrenzi S, Bove F, Mezzadri U, Addevico F, et al.
articles.population: Patients with AO Type C3 sacral fractures and spinopelvic dissociation treated at a Level-1 trauma centre
articles.outcomes: Neurological status, operative parameters, perioperative complications, radiological outcomes, implant-related complications, and implant removal success
articles.take_home: The MIS-Diamond fixation is a safe minimally invasive surgical technique for serious sacral fractures with spinopelvic dissociation, with low complication rates and successful implant removal at 12 months. Only one patient experienced nerve injury and implant-related problems occurred in 12.5% of patients, with no major wound healing complications.

articles.title: Fracture-related infection after operative fixation of acetabular fractures: Incidence and factors independently associated with infection.
articles.authors: Ramesh P, Imran A, Devendra A, M S S, Mogan K, Sp S, et al.
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years or older who had surgery to fix acetabular (hip socket) fractures
articles.outcomes: Fracture-related infection occurred in 27 patients (7.5%). Most infections were diagnosed within 14 days. Risk factors included higher body mass index, longer surgery time, diabetes, and longer time from hospital admission to surgery. Most infected patients (85%) were treated with cleaning, antibiotics, and keeping the implants in place.
articles.take_home: About 1 in 13 patients developed an infection after acetabular fracture surgery. Patients who are overweight, have diabetes, have longer surgery times, or wait longer before surgery have a higher risk of infection.

articles.title: Traumatic hip dislocation: Clinical and epidemiological features, management and prognostic factors in a series of 44 cases from a tertiary centre.
articles.authors: Mencia Gonzalez JP, Sanchez Cozar L, Martinez Alfaro A, Maes ASM, Eckardt Haag ME, Huguet Carmona JL, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 15 years or older with traumatic hip dislocation
articles.outcomes: Complications including sciatic nerve injury, femoral head osteonecrosis, and need for salvage surgery; factors associated with early and late complications
articles.take_home: Traumatic hip dislocation mainly affects young men after road traffic accidents. Prompt reduction within 2 hours was associated with a low rate of bone death, but patients with associated fractures and longer hospital stays had worse outcomes.

articles.title: Intraoperative visualization with 3D fluoroscopy for posterior pelvic fixation is associated with lower cumulative imaging-related radiation exposure.
articles.authors: Tse S, Chinweze RO, Velasco-Castro J, Andring N, Jbeily E, Robinson C, et al.
articles.population: Patients with posterior pelvic ring fractures treated with surgical fixation at a level 1 trauma centre
articles.sample_size: 245 patients (89 with 3D fluoroscopy, 156 with standard fluoroscopy); 119 with follow-up over 3 months
articles.outcomes: Cumulative radiation exposure, intraoperative radiation dose, rates of intraoperative screw changes, reoperation rates
articles.take_home: Using 3D fluoroscopy during pelvic fracture surgery resulted in significantly lower total radiation exposure compared with traditional fluoroscopy and postoperative CT scans. Patients treated with 3D fluoroscopy also needed fewer follow-up operations, though most of these were for planned implant removal rather than complications.

articles.title: Facial burns as functional trauma: Integrating expression, identity and long-term recovery: A narrative review.
articles.authors: Kornhaber R, Beylin D, Cleary M, Goverman J, Haik J
articles.population: Patients with facial burns
articles.outcomes: Functional recovery including facial movement, communication, participation, and psychosocial outcomes; adequacy of existing outcome measurement frameworks
articles.take_home: Facial burns cause long-term problems beyond visible scarring, affecting how people move their face, speak and interact with others. Current ways of measuring recovery do not fully capture these impacts, and patients need coordinated care from multiple specialists to optimise their recovery.

articles.title: Synovial fluid biomarker changes after acute anterior cruciate ligament injury: comparison with primary osteoarthritis as a biological comparator.
articles.authors: Lan J, Zhao W, Gao X, Lin Y, Huang Z
articles.study_type: Observational cohort study comparing synovial fluid biomarkers
articles.population: Patients with acute anterior cruciate ligament injury and patients with primary osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 53 with acute ACL injury, 51 with primary osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Synovial fluid biomarker levels (IL-1beta, sulfated glycosaminoglycans, aggrecan, COMP and others) measured at baseline and one year; knee MRI and radiography at follow-up
articles.take_home: Patients with acute ACL injury show different inflammatory and cartilage breakdown markers in their knee fluid compared to those with established osteoarthritis, but the study could not identify which patients will go on to develop osteoarthritis later. The research suggests five key markers might help distinguish acute ACL injury from chronic osteoarthritis, though these findings need confirmation in other patient groups.

articles.title: A tale of two nails: A retrospective cohort comparison of TFNA and PFNA in proximal femoral fracture fixation.
articles.authors: Leibner G, Gurion R, Mohammad S, Jammal M, Liebergall M, Weill Y
articles.population: Patients with proximal femoral fractures treated at an academic trauma centre
articles.sample_size: 1006 patients (681 PFNA, 325 TFNA) with minimum six-month follow-up
articles.outcomes: Fixation failure requiring reoperation; radiographic assessment of reduction quality, Tip-Apex Distance and blade positioning; biomechanical failure mechanisms
articles.take_home: The TFNA nail had a higher fixation failure rate (3.4%) compared to PFNA (1.6%), but this difference was not statistically significant. The two implants showed different failure patterns: PFNA typically failed by cut-out (91% of failures), whilst TFNA more often failed through medial migration or cut-through (55% of failures).

articles.title: Implementation of a low-cost trauma intake form with real-time clinical decision support: Mixed-methods findings from a stepped-wedge clinical trial in Ghana.
articles.authors: Mesic A, Amponsah-Manu F, Awuku K, Stewart B, Gyedu A
articles.study_type: Hybrid effectiveness-implementation stepped-wedge clinical trial with mixed methods
articles.population: Injured patients treated by non-specialist providers at district and regional hospitals in Ghana
articles.sample_size: 4077 injured patients observed over 17.5 months; 241 clinicians surveyed
articles.outcomes: Trauma intake form adoption rate, acceptability, appropriateness, feasibility, usability, and sustainability
articles.take_home: A low-cost trauma intake form with decision support prompts achieved 85.6% uptake among non-specialist providers in Ghanaian hospitals and was well-accepted by clinicians. To sustain the tool's use, hospitals need to address time pressures, build documentation culture, and clarify that the form is suitable for all injured patients including the most severely ill.
